# opencode-cmd-provider

[![CI](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-cmd-provider)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-cmd-provider)

Use your [Command Code](https://commandcode.ai) plan inside
[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai).

This plugin connects OpenCode to Command Code and adds every Command Code model
to the model picker, so you can use your Go, GOAT, Pro, Max 10×, Max 20×,
Provider, Team, or Enterprise plan from OpenCode. It also adds the **Rates &
usage** panel with your plan's allowances, benchmarks, current deals, and live
usage — a **Command Code** section in the terminal's session sidebar, and a
**Command Code** side-panel tab in the OpenCode desktop app.

<!-- Absolute URL so the image also renders on npmjs.com (docs/ is not published to npm). -->

![OpenCode running a Command Code model, with the Rates & usage panel in the sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/main/docs/images/opencode.png)

> **Disclaimer:** This is an unofficial, community-maintained integration. It is
> not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Command Code. You need your
> own Command Code account, and Command Code's terms, availability, and pricing
> apply.

## Before you start

- **OpenCode** installed — [opencode.ai](https://opencode.ai).
- **A Command Code account and API key** — [commandcode.ai](https://commandcode.ai).

Not sure which OpenCode version you have? Run:

```sh
opencode --version
```

- Prints `1.x` → follow **[Install on OpenCode v1](#install-on-opencode-v1)**.
- Prints `2.x` → follow **[Install on OpenCode v2](#install-on-opencode-v2)**.

Using the **OpenCode desktop app**? It is part of OpenCode v2 — follow
**[Install on OpenCode v2](#install-on-opencode-v2)**, then see
[In the desktop app](#in-the-desktop-app).

## Install on OpenCode v1

```sh
opencode plugin opencode-cmd-provider
```

Run it inside the project where you want the plugin, or add `--global` to make
it available in every project:

```sh
opencode plugin opencode-cmd-provider --global
```

That one command adds the plugin to your OpenCode configuration, registers
Command Code and all of its models, and adds the sidebar section. **Restart
OpenCode** when it finishes.

## Install on OpenCode v2

OpenCode v2 uses a different command — note the `add`:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-cmd-provider
```

This adds the plugin to your global OpenCode configuration, so it works in every
project, registers Command Code and all of its models, and adds the sidebar
section. **Reload OpenCode** when it finishes:

```sh
opencode reload
```

Closing and reopening the TUI is not enough on v2 — the background service keeps
the previously loaded plugin. If the plugin still does not appear, restart the
service with `opencode service restart`.

### In the desktop app

The desktop app picks up the same install. **Quit and reopen the app** after
installing: its windows load the plugin when they start, so an open window
keeps running without it. Once reopened, the `[CMD]` models are in the model
picker and the **Command Code** side-panel tab is available — see
[The panel in the desktop app](#the-panel-in-the-desktop-app).

If an install command fails on your machine, you can add the plugin to your
configuration by hand — see
[Installation mechanics](docs/TECHNICAL.md#installation-mechanics-and-caching) in
the technical reference.

## Connect your Command Code account

### OpenCode v1: sign in from the browser

In OpenCode, run:

```txt
/connect
```

Select **Command Code** in the provider list, then pick how to sign in:

- **Command Code** — the browser flow. Finish the sign-in in your browser; the
  key is stored by OpenCode and reused from then on. Take your time: the plugin
  waits up to five minutes for the browser to hand the key back, so there is no
  rush picking an organization or approving access.
- **Command Code API key** — paste the key the Command Code studio shows you.
  Use this when the browser cannot reach OpenCode's `localhost` callback, for
  example when OpenCode runs on a remote host.

### OpenCode v2: use your API key

OpenCode v2 has no browser sign-in for Command Code. Set your API key before
starting OpenCode:

```sh
export COMMANDCODE_API_KEY="user_..."
```

Or run `/connect` inside OpenCode and paste the key when asked.

### Already signed in with the Command Code CLI?

If you ran `cmd login`, OpenCode reuses that login automatically, so you may not
need to connect at all. The plugin reads it from `~/.commandcode/auth.json`.

This does not cover `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY`, the variable the Command Code CLI
documents for CI and headless use. This plugin reads `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`
instead. Set that one, or run `/connect`.

## Start using it

1. Pick a model: run `/models` and choose any entry starting with `[CMD]`,
   for example `[CMD] Claude Sonnet 5`.
2. Start chatting. Your Command Code plan handles the requests.

Prefer the command line? Run a single prompt without the interactive interface:

```sh
opencode run --model commandcode/claude-sonnet-5 "hello"
```

## What you get

### The Rates & usage panel

While a session uses a `[CMD]` model, OpenCode shows the **Rates & usage**
panel (titled **Command Code**) for that model — in the sidebar of the
terminal interface, and in the side panel of the desktop app:

- **Tier and status** of the model
- **Allowance** — the monthly allowance on each plan
- **Rates** — input, output and cache rates per million tokens, including
  peak/off-peak and context-window bands where Command Code publishes them
- **Other Information** — benchmark scores, current deals and `was`/`now` rates
- **Usage** — your live 5-hour, weekly and monthly usage, and this cycle's
  requests, tokens and spend, refreshed as you work

#### The panel in the terminal

To show, hide or reorder segments, type `/cmd-rates-usage` in the prompt (or
run **Show, hide and reorder sidebar content** from the command palette,
`ctrl+p`). Toggle the sidebar with `ctrl+x b`.

#### The panel in the desktop app

Open a session that uses a `[CMD]` model, then open the **Command Code** tab
either way:

- the **+** menu beside the side-panel tabs, or
- **Show Command Code rates and usage** in the command palette.

Both are offered only while the session's model is a Command Code one; switch
to another provider's model and they disappear until you switch back. Usage
refreshes after each completed turn, and the refresh button in the panel's
header fetches it again on demand.

The desktop tab always shows every segment in the default order. Showing,
hiding and reordering segments (`/cmd-rates-usage`) is available in the
terminal interface only for now.

### Plan and deal summaries

Ask OpenCode something like _"Which Command Code plan am I on?"_ or _"How many
requests does my Command Code plan cover this month?"_ and it uses the built-in
`cmd_plan_summary` tool: the plan and account the current credential resolves
to (or the plan you pinned), its allowances and the current deals, turned into
an estimate. The summary says which credential and account it answered for.

To force a plan instead of detecting it, add it to the question (for example
`plan=pro`) or set `COMMANDCODE_PLAN=pro` before starting OpenCode. A pinned
plan is marked `(pinned)` in the summary.

### Everyday details

- **Reasoning models** show their effort levels in OpenCode, so you can pick how
  hard the model should think.
- **Vision models** accept image input; text-only models will tell you instead of
  silently ignoring the image.
- **Costs** shown in OpenCode are estimates from Command Code's published
  pricing, and some models show `$0` because no price is published for them.
  Check the current
  [Command Code pricing](https://commandcode.ai/docs/resources/pricing-limits)
  before relying on the numbers.
- **Transient failures are retried.** A dropped connection or a temporary server
  error is replayed a couple of times before OpenCode sees a failure, so a blip
  does not end your turn. Permanent answers — a usage-window limit, a rejected
  request — come straight back as errors, and a turn that already streamed text
  is never replayed.

### Your data

The plugin talks only to Command Code: your prompts, the background model-list
refresh, and the usage lookups for the sidebar panel. It sends nothing anywhere
else. To ask Command Code for zero data retention, set `CMD_ZDR=1` before
starting OpenCode, as you would for the Command Code CLI.

## Keep it up to date

A new release only reaches you after OpenCode refreshes its cached copy of the
plugin.

**OpenCode v2:**

```sh
opencode plugin update
```

Then run `opencode reload`, and quit and reopen the desktop app if you use it.

**OpenCode v1:** delete the cached copy and restart OpenCode:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/packages/opencode-cmd-provider*
```

The first start after an update takes a little longer because the plugin is
downloaded again. You never need to sign in again.

New Command Code models usually appear on their own: the plugin refreshes its
model list in the background each time OpenCode starts, so a model launched
after your installed version was published reaches `/models` on the next plugin
load. On OpenCode v2, run `opencode reload` (or `opencode service restart`)
first — closing and reopening the TUI does not reload the background service.
If the model is still missing, the background refresh may be blocked by your
network or disabled via `COMMANDCODE_DISABLE_CATALOG_SYNC`; updating the plugin
is then the fix.

## Uninstall

**OpenCode v2:**

```sh
opencode plugin remove opencode-cmd-provider
```

**OpenCode v1:** remove `opencode-cmd-provider` from the plugin list in your
`opencode.json` (and from `tui.json` if it is listed there).

Then remove the cached copies to free the space — the plugin package
(`npm` on v2, `packages` on v1) and the plugin's saved model list:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/npm/opencode-cmd-provider* ~/.cache/opencode/packages/opencode-cmd-provider* ~/.cache/opencode-cmd-provider
```

The provider and models this plugin registered disappear with it. Quit and
reopen the desktop app, if you use it, to remove the **Command Code** tab.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see                                       | What to try                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No `[CMD]` models in `/models`                     | Check that your API key is set (or that `/connect` succeeded), then reload OpenCode (`opencode reload`, or `opencode service restart` on v2). Update the plugin if your install is old. |
| A newly released model is missing from `/models`   | The catalog refresh applies on plugin load. On v2, run `opencode reload` (or `opencode service restart`) — restarting the TUI alone keeps the old plugin loaded.                        |
| Some Command Code models in `/models` lack `[CMD]` | Update the plugin. On OpenCode v2, older versions kept models.dev's own names for the models it also lists.                                                                             |
| The sidebar has no **Command Code** section        | Make sure the session uses a `[CMD]` model, and press `ctrl+x b` — the sidebar may be hidden.                                                                                           |
| The desktop app has no **Command Code** tab        | Make sure the session uses a `[CMD]` model, then open the tab from the **+** menu or the command palette. If neither offers it, quit and reopen the app after installing or updating.   |
| Browser sign-in fails (v1)                         | Run `/connect` again and pick **Command Code API key** to paste one, or set `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` and restart OpenCode.                                                                 |
| `HTTP 404` on every request                        | Check `provider.commandcode.options.baseURL`. Set it to `https://api.commandcode.ai` — the plugin appends `/provider/v1/…` itself — or remove it.                                       |
| `Your API key has expired`, but the key works      | A `401` now names the credential it used. If it says `legacy file ~/.commandcode/auth.json`, that login is stale — reconnect or set `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`.                              |
| A model shows `$0` cost                            | No published price for that model, so the estimate is `0`. See [Command Code pricing](https://commandcode.ai/docs/resources/pricing-limits).                                            |
| `Command Code rejected this plugin as out of date` | Command Code refuses the version your install reports. Update the plugin — see [Keep it up to date](#keep-it-up-to-date).                                                               |
| Something else                                     | See the [technical reference](docs/TECHNICAL.md#troubleshooting) or [open an issue](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/issues).                                       |

**Highlight — the Rates & usage panel comes to the OpenCode desktop app.** A
session running a `[CMD]` model in the desktop app now has a **Command Code**
side-panel tab with the same allowances, rates, deals and live usage as the
terminal sidebar
([#346](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/346),
ADR-0025). Thanks to [@EthanBlazkowicz](https://github.com/EthanBlazkowicz)
for contributing the desktop support. The release also lands the 2026-11-17
catalog refresh: four new models and a larger GLM-5.3 allowance.

### Features

- **Command Code tab in the OpenCode desktop app**
  ([#346](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/346)):
  the package ships a fourth entry, `./gui-experimental` — one prebuilt
  CommonJS bundle (`dist/gui-experimental.cjs`) that every desktop window
  evaluates. It adds the **Command Code** side-panel tab (the same five
  Rates & usage segments as the TUI sidebar, with live usage over the
  existing plugin-RPC bridge, refreshed after each completed turn and on
  demand from the panel header), a **Show Command Code rates and usage**
  palette command, a **+**-menu launcher, and the panel's stylesheet, themed
  with the app's own tokens. The usage fetch runs in the plugin's server
  half against the session's own server, so the window never handles your
  key. The desktop tab renders the fixed default segment layout; the
  `/cmd-rates-usage` dialog remains the terminal-side way to shape the
  sidebar. Nothing changes for OpenCode v1, the v2 CLI or the TUI.

### Fixes

- **Desktop app 2.3.0 compatibility and launcher gating**
  ([#346](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/346)):
  desktop 2.3.0 keys its model catalog per location, so the panel now looks
  the session's model up by the routed session's location — without it every
  catalog row read `N/A`. The palette command and the **+** menu item are
  offered only while the session's selected model is a Command Code one.
- **Catalog refresh reads the 7-column models page**
  ([#350](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/350)):
  Command Code dropped the Intelligence column from its models page, and the
  parser's shape gate stopped the refresh on the first row. The grammar now
  expects 7 cells, with the rate, band and caps lookups re-indexed. The
  parser never read that column — intelligence scores still come from the
  pricing pages — so no catalog value changes.

### Dependencies

- **Every dependency raised as far as upstream pins allow**
  ([#349](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/349)):
  `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.8 → 0.9, `@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.38,
  `solid-js` 1.9.19, plus `secretlint` 14 and the other dev tools. `zod`
  stays at 4.1.8 (`@opencode-ai/plugin` still depends on it exactly) and
  `solid-js` stays on 1.x (`@opentui/solid` 0.9 still peer-requires it).
  `vite` 8 and `vite-plugin-solid` are new dev dependencies that build the
  desktop bundle.

### Documentation

- **README**: the desktop app gets its own install note, a section on
  opening the **Command Code** tab, update and uninstall steps, and a
  troubleshooting row for a missing tab.

## 0.1.3 - 2026-08-16

Feature: zero-config install via auto-registration from a bundled model snapshot.

- The plugin now bundles a snapshot of the Command Code model catalog (`src/catalog/snapshot.ts`, 55 models) and auto-registers the `commandcode` provider — npm, name, `env`, and every model — during its `config` hook. Installing the plugin is enough: all Command Code models appear in `/models` with the `[CMD]` display-name prefix, no `provider.commandcode` block or `models` map required. No network access is ever needed at runtime.
- Declared config wins: provider-level keys are filled only when unset, declared models are never modified or removed, models that left the catalog stay usable, and `whitelist`/`blacklist` still filter auto-registered models.
- The snapshot is regenerated from the live catalog at every release via `npm run refresh:snapshot` (`scripts/refresh-snapshot.mjs`); newly published models appear after a plugin update.
- Deleted the now-dead network machinery: live catalog fetch and cache (`loadCommandCodeModels`, cache file), the `provider.models` hook, `catalogToOpenCodeModels`, and the `COMMANDCODE_MODELS_*` env vars.
- `COMMANDCODE_API_BASE` now actually overrides the runtime API base (injected as `options.baseURL` when the user declares no `baseURL` of their own).

## 0.1.2 - 2026-08-15

Fix: tool-call history round-trip and reasoning effort. Live probes against the Command Code API with OpenCode confirmed the AI SDK v3 shapes differ from what the converters expected:

- Assistant tool-call parts carry arguments under `input`, not `args`/`arguments` — the converter read the legacy fields, so every prior tool call was re-sent with empty `{}` arguments, corrupting multi-turn context.
- Tool-result outputs use the v3 `{ type: "text" | "error-text" | "json" | "content", ... }` shapes — `resultText` stringified the wrapper, double-encoding results in history. Replaced with `unwrapToolResult`.
- `reasoning_effort` was silently dropped: OpenCode passes `providerOptions` namespaced per provider (`{ commandcode: { reasoningEffort } }`), but the model read the top-level keys. Added `resolveProviderReasoning` (namespaced + top-level fallback) so the configured thinking level actually reaches the API.

Also: remove duplicated README disclaimer; bump `@ai-sdk/provider` to 4.x and `@types/node` to 26.x.

## 0.1.1 - 2026-08-15

Fix: emit `text-start`/`text-end` and `reasoning-start`/`reasoning-end` stream parts. The live Command Code API sends start/end events with ids; the AI SDK's streamText consumer requires them before deltas, so reasoning-capable models (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`) failed with "reasoning part <id> not found".

Initial release: Command Code provider + plugin for OpenCode. Published to npm as `opencode-cmd-provider@0.1.0` (`latest`), tagged `v0.1.0`.

- `createCommandCode(options)` AI SDK provider (LanguageModelV3) + `default` V1 OpenCode plugin module in one package.
- `/connect` browser auth flow, `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` env var, and legacy auth file support (`~/.commandcode/auth.json`, `~/.omp/agent/auth.json`, `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`).
